mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter predicts a contractionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat market at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of 0.4 percentage points or more over two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered months, or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates a persistent contraction in manufacturing output, which correlates with negative equity risk premia and lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages by more than 1% in the same month signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA + 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA + 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered months, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which is associated with lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered periods, or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months during a period when the unemployment rate is below 5% signals a tight labor market, which elevates wage inflation and compresses profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% for three consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5% in the same months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 55% of triggered months, or the median return is not greater than zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the year-over-year growth rate of personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns, such that quarters with above-median GDP growth are associated with positive short-term equity returns.
failure_condition: In more than 60% of quarters with above-median GDPC1 growth, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is not positive, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 5-day returns is not statistically significant at 90% confidence.
